shipped_originals.title_o: Choice of alcohol over a natural reward: an experimental study in light and heavy social drinkers
shipped_originals.authors_o: Karlsson; Mcntyre; Gustavson; Andersson; Szczot; Heilig; Perini

blind_target.title: Alcohol use disorder symptoms are associated with greater relative value ascribed to alcohol, but not greater discounting of costs imposed on alcohol.
blind_target.evidence_quote: Our behavioral findings partially replicate previous results, showing that choice preference for alcohol was affected by the relative value of the alternative reward (Hogarth & Hardy,  2018 ; Karlsson et al.,  2024 ).
blind_target.outcome_quote: Our behavioral findings partially replicate previous results, showing that choice preference for alcohol was affected by the relative value of the alternative reward (Hogarth & Hardy,  2018 ; Karlsson et al.,  2024 ).
blind_target.outcome_reasoning: The authors explicitly describe their behavioral findings as partially replicating the set of results from both cited papers. Relative-cost sensitivity replicated, while the relation between alcohol use severity and alcohol choice did not. The overall partial-replication verdict applies to both named originals.

shipped_originals.title_o: Using the NAART to Estimate WRAT-4 Reading Grade Level in a Predominantly African American Sample

blind_target.evidence_quote: This project was a systematic replication of a study conducted by Jones et al. using a demographically-different sample of participants.
blind_target.outcome_quote: This finding suggests that the original regression equation created by Jones et al. can be applied to the current sample to accurately predict reading level classification.
blind_target.outcome_reasoning: The authors conclude that the original prediction equation applies accurately in the new sample; a different raw-score distribution does not overturn that central result.

blind_target.evidence_quote: This study examined whether outcomes in early intensive behavioral intervention (EIBI) during a university-led multisite project could be replicated by the same community agency independently of the project.
blind_target.outcome_reasoning: The abstract reports favorable new results but neither states the original finding in sufficient detail nor provides an explicit overall replication verdict. The target project is unnamed; no unique reference can be identified from this abstract.

blind_target.title: Consistent and correctable bias in metagenomic sequencing experiments.
blind_target.evidence_quote:

blind_target.authors: Berry, D., Ben Mahfoudh, K., Wagner, M., & Loy, A.
blind_target.title: Barcoded primers used in multiplex amplicon pyrosequencing bias amplification.
blind_target.evidence_quote:
We also find no evidence for ‘tag bias’, which is the hypoth-
esis that the sample-­
identifying nucleotide sequences attached to
PCR primers might promote annealing to some template-­
DNA se-
quences over others, exacerbating taxonomic bias in PCR (e.g. Berry
et al., 2011; O'Donnell et al., 2016).
blind_target.outcome_quote:
We found no evidence for tag bias in PCR amplification. For instance,
under optimal PCR conditions (A & B), pairs using the same tags (A1/
B1, A2/B2, A3/B3) and pairs using different tags (e.g. A1/B2, A2/
B1, A3/B2, …) both generated almost identical NMDS ordinations
(Figure 3). Under non-­
optimal PCRs, we still found no evidence for
tag bias, even though at higher annealing temperatures, some tag
sequences might be more likely to aid primer annealing (Figures S3
and S4). Note that we did not correct the p-­
values for three tests,
underlining the lack of evidence for tag bias.
